title: Dismissing an employee fairly, and the 6-month rule
quick_answer: To dismiss fairly you need one of five fair reasons, a fair process and a decision a reasonable employer could make. From 1 January 2027 most employees can claim unfair dismissal after 6 months' service instead of 2 years, and the cap on compensation is removed. Some dismissals, such as for whistleblowing or pregnancy, are unfair from day one.

glance.label: From 1 January 2027
glance.value: 6 months. Anyone with 6 months' service on that date is protected straight away

glance.label: Which date counts
glance.value: The effective date of termination, which can be pushed later by statutory notice

glance.label: Compensation cap
glance.value: Removed for dismissals with an effective date on or after 1 January 2027

glance.label: Five fair reasons
glance.value: Conduct, capability, redundancy, breaking a legal restriction, or some other substantial reason

mistakes: Assuming probation means the employee can't claim
Forgetting that notice counts towards service, even when you pay in lieu
Deciding the outcome before the hearing
Missing a day-one risk such as a recent whistleblowing complaint or pregnancy
Giving one reason in the letter and another in practice
back_line: Every step in detail, a worked example and answers to common questions.
pack_desc: Key facts, every step to tick off and the mistakes to avoid, on two printable pages.
